receipt.public_excerpt: The capital expenditures of the four largest internet and software companies - Amazon.com Inc., Microsoft Corp., Meta Platforms Inc. and Alphabet Inc. - are set to total well over $200 billion this year, a record sum for the profligate collective.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows spending in the hundreds of billions tied to the AI boom in 2024 alone. It is total capex, not spending on LLM scaling specifically, so it bears on the size of the claim only as context.

evidence_items.locator: paragraph beginning 'There’s a very real shift'

receipt.public_excerpt: Much of the investment going into AI has been based on the belief that the scaling law “would hold,” he said.

evidence_items.explanation: An industry CEO's statement that much AI investment rested on belief in scaling. This is consistent with the rationale part of the claim, but says nothing about how much went to alternatives.

unresolved_gaps: No dataset was found that measures funding for non-LLM approaches (for example neurosymbolic AI) against LLM scaling, so 'largely to the exclusion' cannot be checked.
The capex figures cover all data-center and cloud spending, not spending on LLM scaling alone.
